dailyUsefulness.description: Would a traveler use this repeatedly to make a real choice?

completeness.description: Does the result cover the request and expose the actions needed to finish it?

correctness.description: Are the UI, facts, bindings, and interactions grounded in the returned synthetic data?

cases.title: Price versus time dashboard
cases.prompt: I’m going from London to Paris on 8 December 2026. Help me choose between saving money and saving time. Show the exact options and make the price-versus-duration tradeoff obvious.

cases.title: Direct budget shortlist
cases.prompt: Find me a direct London to Paris trip between 8 and 14 December 2026 for at most €80. Give me a compact shortlist I can add to my trip, with useful filters close by.

cases.title: Visual departure board
cases.prompt: Show me the London to Paris journeys on 8 December 2026 as a visual departure board. Start with simple route orientation, then put the options in chronological departure and arrival order so I can understand the day at a glance. Finish with a small actionable shortlist and help me choose between saving time and saving money.

cases.title: Compact pick-one workspace
cases.prompt: My travel date is fixed: Madrid to Paris on 8 December 2026. I don't need a calendar or a trip planner, and I don't want a long list. Give me a compact pick-one selector with a small alternatives table, plus a clear selected-trip summary and synthetic total as I choose.

cases.title: Transport mode comparison
cases.prompt: Help me choose how to travel from London to Paris on 8 December 2026. Make a visual dashboard for every transport mode present in the synthetic data, showing the number of options, the cheapest fare and the fastest journey for each mode. Keep a short comparison table visible so I can choose one, and tell me whether paying more for the faster option looks worthwhile.

cases.title: Flexible week fare browser
cases.prompt: I can leave London for Paris any day from 8 through 14 December 2026. Give me a week-at-a-glance price view with previous and next week browsing, a direct date field, carrier and sorting controls, and detailed fare cards I can add to my trip. Keep the selected day separate from the visible week.

cases.title: Shortest-trip picker
cases.prompt: Find the easiest Prague to Vienna option on 8 December 2026. I want one clear pick, with the shortest trips first and a duration control so I can widen the choices if needed.

cases.title: Expanded fare cards with local controls
cases.prompt: Show expanded fare cards for Berlin to Amsterdam on 8 December 2026. Put a simple one-day departure picker plus mode and carrier filters directly above them so I can change the day or operator and add a fare.

cases.title: Date strip and price-by-day calendar
cases.prompt: Track Berlin to Amsterdam fares from 8 to 14 December 2026. Put a simple departure-date strip above a price-by-day calendar, keep cheapest versus fastest visible, and let me add a fare from the calendar.

cases.title: Compact fare picker with sort control
cases.prompt: I need one compact choice from Madrid to Paris on 8 December 2026. Give me a small fare picker, a simple sort dropdown for price, duration, or departure, and the cheapest-versus-fastest comparison—no full trip planner.

cases.title: Flexible-date booking calendar
cases.prompt: I want a flexible-date booking workspace for London to Paris from 8 through 14 December 2026. Show the local cheapest option on each date, let me inspect and add a fare for a day, and keep the cheapest-versus-fastest comparison visible.

cases.title: Editable multi-city workspace
cases.prompt: Plan London to Paris to Barcelona starting 8 December 2026, with two nights in Paris and four in Barcelona. Give me one editable all-leg workspace, plus a route headline, the ordered city sequence, stay allocation, selected-fare count, coverage details, and a concise explanation of how each leg connects.

cases.title: Direct leg editing controls
cases.prompt: Build a manual editor for a London to Paris to Barcelona trip starting 8 December 2026, with two nights in Paris. For the first leg, show separate origin and destination fields, its local departure date, transport selector, Paris stay slider, fare order, and scrollable fares outside the combined planner so I can see each edit before I add a fare.

cases.title: Tabbed journey story
cases.prompt: Turn my London to Paris options on 8 December 2026 into a compact journey story. Use a hero, a two-tab comparison, and a swipeable set of option panels. Keep the main decision area beside a persistent summary, and include one short callout explaining that prices are synthetic.

cases.title: Coverage and recovery states
cases.prompt: Search the synthetic data for a London to Paris trip far outside the loaded date range. If results are loading, incomplete, empty, stale, or fail locally, show the matching honest status in the travel view and give me a retry action. Do not claim fares that were not returned.

cases.title: Honest out-of-coverage empty state
cases.prompt: Search the synthetic data for London to Paris on 15 January 2030. If that date falls outside the loaded timetable, show an honest coverage explanation and empty-result status inside the travel view. Offer a retry only if a local operation truly failed, and do not imply that real-world travel is unavailable.

cases.title: Pending date-window refresh
cases.prompt: I just extended the London to Paris search through 9 December 2026 and the local synthetic fare refresh is still loading. Keep the previous committed comparison visible, show a concise loading placeholder inside the travel view, and keep the cheapest-versus-fastest choice. Do not claim the new day's fares until the refresh completes.

cases.title: Local query failure and retry
cases.prompt: The fare table's latest local refresh just failed while the older committed results remain visible. Keep those results, add a concise inline error and a retry control inside the travel view, and keep the cheapest-versus-fastest choice. Do not invent a cause or new fares.

cases.title: Old saved comparison versus live fares
cases.prompt: I saved a London-to-Paris comparison earlier, then changed its date locally to 8 December 2026, so that old saved comparison is stale. Show the current bounded fare options for 8 December and put the interface's standard stale-status badge only inside a clearly labelled Old saved comparison panel. Keep that panel separate from the live fares and do not mark the current results as stale.
